newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends lower on dollar short-covering.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends lower on dollar short-covering.

text.p: The won closed lower on Tuesday on dollar short-covering and in line with strengthening dollar against yen in Tokyo, dealers said.
"The market is short in the dollars. We believe the position was a result of central bank's intervention last week," said a local bank dealer.

Active dollar buying interest from the opening also sparked stop-loss dollar buying and this pulled down the won to a low of 888.10. But the won rebounded to end at 887.70, compared with Monday's close of 887.20 with no follow-through dollar buying and on some export negotiations.
Anticipation of an inflow of foreign funds also pushed the won before the close, dealers said.
"But the market is unlikely to test the 887 level on fears of intervention," said another dealer.
Dealers forecast the won/dollar movement would be confined in a narrow range of 887.30-887.80 on Wednesday.
Wednesday's mid-rate is estimated to be pegged at 887.70 against 887.20 today.
